intro: A number series is a list of numbers that follows a hidden rule. Find the rule, then use it to fill in the missing number.

tips.title: Start with the differences
tips.body: Write the gap between each pair of neighbours under the series. If the gaps are equal, grow by a fixed amount, or are squares/cubes, you've found the rule.
tips.caption: Equal jumps? That's your rule.

tips.title: Big jumps? Think × or powers
tips.body: If the numbers grow very fast, try ×2, ×3 (maybe with +1 or −1), or compare with squares (1, 4, 9, 16…) and cubes (1, 8, 27, 64…).
tips.caption: Shooting up fast? Multiply or square.

tips.title: Getting smaller? Think ÷ or −
tips.body: If the numbers shrink, try dividing by 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, or subtracting 2, 3, 4…. Reading the series from the right can make it easier.
tips.caption: Shrinking? Read it backwards.

tips.title: Up, down, up, down? Two series
tips.body: When the numbers zig-zag, split the series into odd places (1st, 3rd, 5th…) and even places (2nd, 4th, 6th…). Each part has its own rule.
tips.caption: Zig-zag? It's two series in one.

tips.title: Know your special numbers
tips.body: Even: 2, 4, 6… Odd: 1, 3, 5… Prime: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13… Squares and cubes up to 20² and 10³. Spotting one near a number saves a lot of time.
tips.caption: Spot a special number, save time.

tips.title: Always check your answer
tips.body: Put your answer in the blank and check that the rule still works for the number after it. That quick check catches most mistakes.
tips.caption: Plug it in, then check the next gap too.
